newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria sees no quick return to Ogoni.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria sees no quick return to Ogoni.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell's Nigeria unit said on Monday it saw no immediate return to producing in the volatile homeland of ethnic Ogonis after a meeting last week with local representatives.
"The tone of the meeting was positive, but there is no immediate prospect of a return to production in Ogoni," a Shell spokesman told Reuters in Lagos.
"Our emphasis remains the same which is to help the community and clean up oil spills and progress further down the road in time."

The spokesman said there was no direct representative of the radical Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples (MOSOP) at the meeting, which was organised by the military government's National Reconciliation Committee.
MOSOP claims to represent the majority of the 500,000 strong Ogoni community and analysts say that for Shell to return to Ogoniland would require MOSOP approval.
"While there was no direct representative of MOSOP there were those who expressed a similar point of view," the spokesman said.
Shell has been under pressure from campaigners since the 1995 execution of author and former MOSOP leader Ken Saro Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists.
When Shell pulled out of Ogoniland after acts of sabotage in 1993 production stood at 20,000 bpd out of an estimated potential 28,000 bpd.
